content.inline:
# CAD3 — the encoding of Convex data

Every Convex value — on the network and in the lattice Brightside itself runs on — is a **cell** with exactly one byte encoding, and every encoding denotes exactly one value. Because the mapping is one-to-one, a value's identity is simply the **SHA3-256 hash of its encoding**: its **value ID**. The same data always has the same ID, wherever it was made.

## Structure

- The first byte of an encoding is a **tag** saying what kind of value follows; an undefined tag is rejected. An encoding is at most **16,383 bytes**, so any cell fits a fixed buffer.
- Cells reference other cells, forming a **Merkle DAG**: a reference carries the child's value ID, so a root hash commits to everything beneath it.
- A small child (**140 bytes or less**) is **embedded** inside its parent's encoding; a larger one is a **branch**, referenced by ID and fetched separately. A cell is never both — that would give a parent two encodings. Embedding is why `[1 2 3 4 5]` is one encoding rather than six, and why embedded values cost no memory allowance (costs).
- Only roots and branches are generally stored; an embedded cell has no life of its own, so navigate down from a known root rather than looking an intermediate ID up.

## Validity

An encoding is valid only if some cell produces exactly those bytes: no trailing bytes, no truncation, no unknown tags, no redundant leading bytes on an integer. Random or hostile bytes are therefore almost always invalid and can be discarded cheaply — a property peers depend on. One nuance: every 64-bit pattern of a double is a distinct valid value (each NaN payload included); the CVM normalises results to one canonical `##NaN`, but that is a value-layer coercion, never a decoder rule. Values an implementation does not understand are relayed intact, not dropped — CAD3 is extensible by design.

## Why it matters

- **Comparison is a hash compare.** Two lattice values are equal if their IDs match — that is how Brightside notices a changed conversation without reading it.
- **Sharing is by reference.** A hash names data unambiguously across peers, venues and time; content is fetched once and de-duplicated network-wide.
- **Consensus-visible.** A change to the encoding moves every state hash, so encoding rules change only under a protocol version — never casually.
- **Blobs** are raw byte values (`0x…` in source); hashes, keys and signatures are blobs.

Specification: CAD003 (`encoding`); the reference encoder lives in `convex-core` (`CVMEncoder`, `CVMTag`). For the data model built on top — cursors, merge, replication — load convex-lattice.
